SPOİLERR Şimdi filmin asıl konusu, uzaylıların kendi dilleri aracılığıyla insanların zaman algısını değiştirip geçmiş, gelecek ve şimdiyi aynı anda algılamamızı sağlaması. Louise onların dilini çözdükçe beyninin zaman algılama şekli değişiyor ve böylece ilk sahnelerde kızının ölümünü gösterdiği yerlerin geçmiş değil, aslında gelecekten kesitler olduğunu anlıyoruz. Sonrasında Louise geleceği, kızının öleceğini ve çok büyük bir acı yaşayacağını bildiği halde geleceği değiştirmiyor. Ian ile yine evleniyor, Hannah doğuyor, hastalanıyor ve ölüyor vesaire. Yani bu hayatı yaşamayı seçiyor. Sonunun kötü olacağını bilse bile bu süreçte yaşayacağı mutluluğu seçiyor ve kaybedeceğini bilerek kızıyla geçirdiği her anın tadını çıkarıyor. Özgür irade ile kader arasındaki bağlamın ortadan kalkması ama Louise’in özgür iradesiyle yine aynı kaderi seçmesi bence filmin verdiği en güzel mesajlardan biri. Çünkü gelecekte ne olacağını bilmek, o hayatı yaşamaya değmez hale getirmiyor. Ama ben filmin bunu yansıtış biçimini ve olay örgüsünü hiç beğenmedim. Bilimkurgu işin içine girince beklenti de ister istemez artıyor ve film sonunda bende biraz fıss çıktı. Özellikle uzaylı temasının kullanılışını çok sevmedim. Bazı yerlerde mantık hataları ve zorlama çözümler olduğunu düşündüm. Çin bakanının fikrinin değişmesi falan da bana aşırı saçma geldi. Yani anlam bakımından gerçekten çok güzel bulduğum bir film ama bunu işleyiş şekli bana göre değildi. Bence verdiği mesaj çok daha farklı ve çok daha etkileyici bir şekilde işlenebilirdi. Bu yüzden filmi anlam bakımından beğensem bile genel olarak çok overrated olduğunu düşünüyorum.

Arrival: Villeneuve's (failed) Space Odyssey Look, I'm not going to come out and say that this is a bad film, because it clearly isn't, but I would hesitate to say that it's a good film as well. Day by day, my feelings that we as a species should have retired the sci-fi drama genre after Solaris (1972) grow. To be perfectly frank, I felt nothing from this film, one that definitely earned the description of, "a mile wide, and an inch deep." It attempts to tackle so many things at once that it eventually lacks any true identity and fails to separate itself from similar pictures of the 2010's. Even starting the film, I was immediately hit with a rushed, melodramatic sequence of our protagonist and her daughter all throughout her life, which ended before I could even form a thought. Why even include it? Does it serve any purpose besides telling me, "You are going to watch a drama. This will be sad. Feel sad for this person." I will give credit where it's due. The cinematography is obviously gorgeous and is by far my favorite aspect of the film. The sound design and score are both ominous and melancholy. However, I don't love the production value as a whole, because the incredibly dull color palette is a bore to look at. The set design of the military base was also quite bland. The alien itself was without a doubt beautifully surreal, and the scenes of Banks/Donelly attempting to communicate with them are easily my favorites in the film. Even the concepts alone are quite fascinating and even well-executed at times, but I can't help but get the feeling that I've seen this film before. There are so many aspects that are completely run-of-the-mill, such as Banks' "tragic backstory," which we learn later in the film is actually after the main events. Yes, I thought the "recalling the future" concept was quite cool, but it ultimately accomplishes nothing but feel emotionally manipulative yet cold at the same time. Seriously though, how many characters are there in the sci-fi genre that are nearly identical to Banks? A lonely, alienated melancholic genius that gets brought in to "solve the mystery," while everyone else distrusts her and treat her with hostility. She really fits right in with the crowd. I just can't stand the execution of so much of this film. The exposition was actually quite intriguing, but I got to the second act of the film and was fighting the urge to fall asleep. Was it trying to bore me on purpose? I enjoyed the third act much more than the second, as that's when the stakes really raise and we get a bit of well-done suspense. It sucks, because that's when I really felt how much potential this film had! The ending montage didn't do it for me though. Every science fiction film nowadays does this to make it seem "emotional," but it ends up just feeling extremely forced. Without a doubt my least favorite from Villeneuve at the moment, but you never know... perhaps a rewatch could boost it all the way to the top, and I realize how it's secretly a masterpiece. But then again, perhaps not. Not a bad film, but not an especially good one either.

I couldn't enjoy it, I couldn't really connect with it, and it felt like every beautiful thing about it reached me and then just disappeared inside me without leaving any trace. And it's not because the movie is bad. Not at all. The problem is me, and the state I was in while watching it. I'm going through a really bad time mentally right now. I'm depressed, and I feel like something inside me has been switched off for a while. Even things that are supposed to make me happy don't really do anything anymore. It feels like my brain has forgotten how to produce any good feelings, like my happiness hormones have completely dried up. I watch things, listen to music, talk to people, try to live my days normally, but inside there's just this heavy emptiness that I don't even know how to describe. And what hurts the most is knowing that this movie could have made me happy under different circumstances. I know its atmosphere is beautiful, and I know it's a movie that deserves to be appreciated, but I watched it when I simply didn't have the ability to enjoy anything. People always say that your rating of a movie can depend on your mood when you watch it, and I think that's really true. My mood wasn't just bad at the time. I was already drowning in so many things that even the simplest things started feeling heavy. Even getting treatment has become another thing that hurts. I need antidepressants, but I can't afford them right now. I don't have enough money to buy them, and it feels like every time I try to find something that might help me get out of this state, another problem appears in front of me and stops me. And on top of all that, my mom and I are living with the feeling that even having a safe place to live is temporary. We're going to be kicked out of our home soon because it's an inherited property and it's going to be sold. This place where we've lived, the place that at least gave us the feeling that we had somewhere to come back to, won't be ours anymore. After that, my mom and I will have to look for somewhere else to live, and we might have to move to the countryside outside the city because her share of the inheritance will barely be enough to buy a small house there. And I honestly don't know what happens after that. Maybe another exhausting journey begins, looking for a way to make a living, trying to afford the simplest things, and constantly worrying about what tomorrow is going to bring. Sometimes it feels like life doesn't even give us a chance to catch our breath. Every time one problem ends, another one appears. Every time we try to stand back up, we find ourselves having to start from zero again. I know I went completely off-topic from the movie 🙃, and maybe none of this even belongs on Letterboxd, but I don't know where else to put all these thoughts anymore. I don't have someone I can sit with and tell everything I'm feeling without feeling like I'm becoming a burden, so I started venting about my problems on Twitter and Letterboxd, writing things that probably have nothing to do with what I'm posting, just because I need to get some of it out of me. So yes I did this movie dirty. And maybe if I had watched it at another time, I would've given it four stars or even more. But I watched it as a completely different person, someone tired, sad, unable to enjoy things, and carrying things much heavier than a movie. Maybe that's why I couldn't see its beauty the way I should have. I'm sorry movie. I really did you dirty. But at that moment, all I had to give you was my terrible mood and my heart full of all these things.

Tive que reassistir pra um trabalho da disciplina de História do Direito. Eu tinha a memória de não gostar do filme, então já estava com uma expectativa bem abaixo do normal. Terminei de assistir e, particularmente, continuo não curtindo tanto. Acho tanto a ficção científica quanto o drama fracos. A geopolítica desse filme é engraçada pra mim porque eu acho quase impossível imaginar os Estados Unidos mantendo uma postura tão apaziguadora se esse cenário fictício fosse real. Mesmo assim, Arrival permite algumas boas reflexões. Como acabei escrevendo um ensaio crítico sobre ele para a disciplina, deixo aqui algumas das coisas que pensei a partir do filme: Uma das coisas que achei mais interessantes pensando no filme pela perspectiva da História do Direito é que a escrita, embora permita preservar e transmitir uma norma para além do momento em que ela foi produzida, não garante que ela será compreendida corretamente. Isso aparece no próprio filme quando um mesmo símbolo dos heptapods é interpretado por equipes diferentes como “arma” ou “ferramenta”, quase desencadeando um conflito internacional. Um vestígio escrito precisa ser reconstruído, interpretado e contextualizado e é justamente aí que podem surgir divergências. É nesse processo que a escrita, em conjunto com a oralidade, compõe o sistema linguístico que é utilizado para a compreensão do fenômeno jurídico e das civilizações através dos séculos. Ao entrar em contato com uma forma distinta de organizar e atribuir sentido à realidade, a linguagem apresenta um papel essencial, e é dever do historiador do direito considerar essa nuance.

Το Arrival είναι ακριβώς το vibe που γουστάρω σε τέτοιες ταινίες, έστω κι αν σε κάποια σημεία νιώθεις ότι πάει λίγο αργά. Το πιο δυνατό του χαρτί είναι ότι βγάζει εντελώς από το κάδρο τις κλασικές χολιγουντιανές φόρμουλες. Δεν έχει ούτε λέιζερ, ούτε εκρήξεις, ούτε τον πλανήτη να σώζεται στο παραπέντε. Είναι μια ταινία που εστιάζει καθαρά στο πώς στο διάολο καταφέρνεις να επικοινωνήσεις με κάτι που δεν έχει καμία λογική σχέση με την ανθρώπινη φύση. Οπτικά και ηχητικά η ατμόσφαιρα σε πλακώνει. Αυτά τα τεράστια, μονόλιθα σκάφη που απλά αιωρούνται σιωπηλά και ο απόκοσμος ήχος στο background χτίζουν μια συνεχή ένταση, χωρίς να γίνεται τίποτα υπερβολικό στην οθόνη. Εκεί που πραγματικά με κέρδισε, όμως, είναι στο πώς χειρίζεται το θέμα του χρόνου. Παίζει με την ιδέα του ότι η γλώσσα που μαθαίνεις αλλάζει τον τρόπο που αντιλαμβάνεσαι την ίδια την πραγματικότητα, και τελικά το χρησιμοποιεί για να σου ρίξει ένα πολύ βαρύ ψυχολογικό χτύπημα. Αντί για κάποιο φθηνό plot twist με εξωγήινους, η ταινία καταλήγει να σε βάζει να σκεφτείς κάτι πολύ πιο ανθρώπινο: αν θα επέλεγες να ζήσεις μια ιστορία από την αρχή, ξέροντας ακριβώς πώς και πόσο άσχημα πρόκειται να τελειώσει. Ναι, ο ρυθμός του είναι αρκετά αργός και θέλει λίγη υπομονή, αλλά ο τρόπος που κουμπώνουν όλα τα κομμάτια στο φινάλε σε αποζημιώνει στο εκατό τοις εκατό.

All the actual science is just for show, the linguistics is just a framework. One of the most human sci-fi’s i’ve ever seen. my fascination with linguistics actually made this movie so much more of an interesting watch. I learned about the sapir-whorf hypothesis which essentially is the idea that language can fundamentally alter the structure of thought and even your perception of reality. the movie then takes this incredibly intellectual concept and turns it into something so human. Louise knows the beginning, the middle and the end simultaneously. she knows she will have a daughter she loves beyond comprehension, she knows she will lose her, she knows her marriage will fall apart partly because of the choice she makes but she still chooses that life. Her choice wasn’t solely because “love is worth the pain.” But does something ending tragically make the happiness that precedes it any less real? if you knew exactly when and how you would lose someone, would loving them become meaningless? or would knowing how temporary it is make every moment with them infinitely more precious? The ultimate choice was choosing to live the entire experience, regardless of its ending. there’s something so beautiful yet terrifying about accepting your life as a whole rather than judging it solely by where it leads. Can’t stop thinking about this movie. Would I  willingly walk into the greatest grief of my life just to experience the love that comes before it? Eu adoro filmes que conseguem pegar uma ideia de ficção científica e, em vez de usá-la apenas como espetáculo, transformar essa ideia em uma discussão sobre algo profundamente humano. A Chegada faz exatamente isso. É um filme sobre alienígenas, linguagem, comunicação e uma possível ameaça à humanidade, mas, no fundo, é muito mais sobre tempo, escolhas e a maneira como lidamos com aquilo que sabemos que vai acontecer. A linguagem é o verdadeiro coração do filme. Conforme Louise aprende a se comunicar com os heptápodes , percebemos que não estamos simplesmente acompanhando alguém traduzindo palavras. Ela está tentando compreender uma forma completamente diferente de enxergar o mundo. A ideia de que a língua que falamos pode influenciar a maneira como percebemos a realidade é fascinante, e o filme leva isso até uma consequência muito maior: e se aprender uma nova linguagem significasse aprender uma nova maneira de experimentar o próprio tempo? É aí que A Chegada deixa de ser apenas um filme de primeiro contato e se transforma em algo muito mais emocional. A maneira como o filme apresenta as lembranças de Louise é genial porque, durante boa parte da história, acreditamos estar vendo o passado dela. Aos poucos, percebemos que aquelas imagens não são exatamente memórias. E quando a verdade finalmente se revela, várias cenas anteriores mudam completamente de significado. O mais doloroso é perceber que Louise passa a conhecer o futuro e, mesmo sabendo que determinadas coisas vão acontecer, decide vivê-las. Ela sabe que haverá amor, felicidade, mas também sabe que haverá uma dor enorme. E mesmo assim escolhe seguir em frente. Isso transforma a pergunta do filme. Não é mais “se você pudesse conhecer o futuro, tentaria mudá-lo?” , mas “se você soubesse que algo maravilhoso terminaria em sofrimento, ainda escolheria vivê-lo?” E acho essa uma das ideias mais bonitas e tristes que um filme poderia explorar. Louise não escolhe porque não entende o que vai acontecer. Ela escolhe justamente porque entende. O sofrimento não apaga o valor de tudo aquilo que veio antes. Também gosto muito de como o filme utiliza a própria estrutura narrativa para fazer o espectador experimentar, de certa forma, aquilo que Louise está experimentando. O tempo deixa de ser uma linha simples de começo, meio e fim. Informações que pareciam pertencer ao passado ganham outro significado quando descobrimos que pertencem ao futuro. É um daqueles filmes em que a segunda metade não apenas explica a primeira: ela transforma a primeira. E visualmente A Chegada acompanha perfeitamente essa proposta. Os ambientes são enormes, silenciosos e quase contemplativos. A presença dos alienígenas causa estranheza sem precisar transformar tudo em espetáculo. A trilha de J óhann Jóhannsson também contribui muito para essa atmosfera de mistério e melancolia. No fim, A Chegada me pega porque utiliza a ficção científica para fazer uma pergunta extremamente humana: se pudéssemos conhecer toda a nossa história antes de vivê-la, escolheríamos vivê-la mesmo assim? E a resposta de Louise é ao mesmo tempo devastadora e bonita.
